novelty.summary: Two absent DAFx sources were read in full. The update separates isolated-track tonal normalization, coarse spectral overlap and psychoacoustic masking, and adds two fully transcript-grounded rhythm-guitar video cards.
novelty.publication_vs_discovery: Both papers predate discovery on 2026-09-16; they are added because the shared base lacked them, not presented as new publications.

source_cards.title: Automatic Equalization for Individual Instrument Tracks Using Convolutional Neural Networks
source_cards.bounded_summary: The paper classifies an isolated instrument, subtracts its time-averaged spectrum from an instrument-class average target, smooths the difference and predicts a static four-band parametric EQ. A two-stage differentiable spectral-loss model improves target-reconstruction MAE, and isolated loudness-normalized tracks were preferred in an internal blind comparison.
limitations: The listener heard isolated tracks, not full arrangements, despite being asked about likely mix fit.
Time averaging removes section, articulation and intermittent-collision information.
The 35-class instrument classifier reports 79 percent accuracy, so target selection can fail before EQ.
The test population was internal and no rock-specific full-mix result was reported.
Training and search parameter bounds are not engineering presets.

source_cards.title: Improved Control for Selective Minimization of Masking Using Inter-Channel Dependency Effects
source_cards.bounded_summary: The real-time cross-adaptive effect preserves a selected master channel and applies full-band attenuation to other channels according to coarse spectral-class similarity. The dependency measure is useful as a controllable diagnostic but does not embed a psychoacoustic masking model.
limitations: The 1024-point FFT analysis uses no window and quantized spectral-bin comparisons.
Gain correction is full-band rather than frequency selective.
No listening experiment establishes preference or full-mix improvement.
The authors list psychoacoustic masking-model integration as future work.

knowledge_cards.title: Isolated-track tonal normalization is not de-masking
knowledge_cards.claim: Matching an isolated track to an instrument-class average can improve a tonal proposal but cannot establish its role or audibility in a full arrangement.

knowledge_cards.title: Average spectrum suppresses musical time
knowledge_cards.claim: Time-averaged spectra cannot distinguish a persistent tonal imbalance from a collision limited to palm mutes, phrases or one section.

knowledge_cards.title: Spectral similarity is not psychoacoustic masking
knowledge_cards.claim: A coarse overlap score omitting calibrated audibility, temporal coincidence and psychoacoustic thresholds must not be labeled as measured masking.

knowledge_cards.title: Target-selection error propagates into EQ
knowledge_cards.claim: Automatic EQ must stop or expose uncertainty when instrument classification or target selection is ambiguous.

knowledge_cards.title: Whole-channel attenuation can solve the wrong problem
knowledge_cards.claim: When a collision is local in frequency or time, full-band attenuation may damage musical balance and section role.

knowledge_cards.title: Static versus dynamic action follows persistence
knowledge_cards.claim: Stable tonal errors are candidates for static EQ; intermittent collisions require an unchanged baseline and may justify bounded dynamic action only after level and pan checks.

knowledge_cards.title: EQ comparison requires gain compensation
knowledge_cards.claim: Cuts and boosts change signal level, so contextual A/B must compensate loudness before preference is interpreted.

knowledge_cards.title: Source tone and restrained processing are explicit baselines
knowledge_cards.claim: A processed-guitar candidate must be compared with source-tone revision and a lighter chain, not only with the current dense chain.

knowledge_cards.title: Protected source follows section role
knowledge_cards.claim: Masking control must not assign permanent global priority to vocal or lead; in a chorus, rhythm guitars may be the protected foundation and the lead a complement.

rule_candidates.title: Level and role before de-masking EQ
rule_candidates.when_to_apply: Two sources appear to collide in a defined section.
rule_candidates.what_to_change: First compare unchanged with the smallest role-aware level and pan move; open an EQ branch only if the collision remains.

proposed_range.origin: conservative project A/B grid, not a published norm

rule_candidates.how_to_verify: Loudness-match variants and compare full mix, mono and adjacent sections.
rule_candidates.cancel_when: Level/pan performs as well as EQ or the protected foundation weakens.

rule_candidates.title: Instrument average is a proposal, not a destination
rule_candidates.when_to_apply: An isolated source is broadly dull, harsh or unbalanced and classification is confident.
rule_candidates.what_to_change: Generate a static tonal candidate from the class prior but retain unchanged and manual role-aware branches.

proposed_range.origin: paper supplies model bounds only; no project range accepted

rule_candidates.how_to_verify: Listen in full arrangement and compare section-specific role, not only target-spectrum error.
rule_candidates.cancel_when: Classification is uncertain, the source is intentionally atypical, or target match worsens mix fit.

rule_candidates.title: Choose static or dynamic EQ by persistence
rule_candidates.when_to_apply: A collision is confirmed across labelled verse, chorus and articulation windows.
rule_candidates.what_to_change: Use static EQ only for stable tonal excess; for intermittent collision test dynamic attenuation capped at 0/1/2/3 dB.
rule_candidates.how_to_verify: Event-labelled gain trace plus loudness-matched full-mix and mono A/B.
rule_candidates.cancel_when: Action persists outside the collision, pumps, thins the source, or does not beat static/unchanged.

rule_candidates.title: Stop on target uncertainty
rule_candidates.when_to_apply: Automatic instrument or section-role classification selects a spectral target.
rule_candidates.what_to_change: Expose confidence and require manual target confirmation for ambiguous or mixed sources.

proposed_range.origin: must be calibrated on project validation data

rule_candidates.how_to_verify: Class/role confusion audit with correct, adjacent and intentionally wrong targets.
rule_candidates.cancel_when: Confidence is uncalibrated or no reliable class/role exists.

rule_candidates.title: Do not label overlap as masking
rule_candidates.when_to_apply: A metric reports spectral dependency or overlap.
rule_candidates.what_to_change: Name it overlap/dependency unless calibrated audibility, timing and psychoacoustic assumptions are present.

proposed_range.origin: no validated masking threshold in the source

rule_candidates.how_to_verify: Hold spectral overlap similar while varying level, timing and pan; compare metric with listening.
rule_candidates.cancel_when: A validated project-specific psychoacoustic model and listening calibration replace the proxy.

rule_candidates.title: Section role controls priority
rule_candidates.when_to_apply: A masking controller needs a protected source.
rule_candidates.what_to_change: Select the protected source per section and phrase; never default globally to vocal or lead.
rule_candidates.how_to_verify: Role annotations plus blind full-song review across transitions.
rule_candidates.cancel_when: Role is ambiguous or sources intentionally fuse into one texture.

rule_candidates.title: Gain-match EQ demonstrations
rule_candidates.when_to_apply: An EQ cut or boost is evaluated by preference.
rule_candidates.what_to_change: Compensate comparison level without peak-normalizing and retain the unchanged branch.

proposed_range.origin: must follow the established project loudness-matching protocol

rule_candidates.how_to_verify: Blind randomized A/B at fixed monitor level and inspect peaks separately.
rule_candidates.cancel_when: Level matching changes limiter behavior or cannot be performed independently of the tested EQ.
